title: Wave watching: count the waves
description: Sit safely on the sand with a grown-up and watch the sea. Count the waves, spot the biggest one, and see if you can guess when the next big one will come.

body.heading: Waves are made by wind
paragraphs: Waves start as wind blowing over the water. The wind pushes the top of the sea into bumps, and the bumps travel along as waves, all the way to the beach.
Sit on the dry sand and watch. Some waves are small and gentle. Some are tall and crash with a big splash of white foam.

body.heading: Play the counting game
paragraphs: Count the waves out loud as they crash: one, two, three. Can you count ten? Now try to guess: will the next wave be a big one or a small one? Shout your guess before it lands.
Waves often come in groups. Watch for a pattern of small, small, BIG — then see if the pattern comes again. The sea loves patterns, but it also loves surprises.

takeaway: Wind makes the waves, and waves love patterns: sit on the dry sand, count them as they crash, and guess whether the next one will be big or small.
ageGuidance: Ages 4–8, always with a grown-up sitting right beside the child.
materials: A beach or a safe place to watch the sea
Optional: a notebook to mark each wave you count
supervision: A grown-up must sit with the child the whole time, on dry sand well away from the water's edge. This is a watching game only — nobody goes into the water.
safetyNotes: Stay on dry sand, far from the water, and never turn your back on the sea — waves can come in further than you expect.
Never climb on wet rocks or go near the edge of piers and harbour walls.
Wear sun protection and take breaks in the shade on sunny days.
screenFreeExtension: Back home, draw your favourite wave from the day — the biggest one — and write its number underneath: was it wave number three, or wave number ten?
